To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the relative contribution (direct versus indirect pathway) of hepatic glycogenesis to glucose disposal is dependent on plasma glucose concentration and is determined by the rate of endogenous glucose production.

the relative contribution to glycogen synthesis of the direct versus the indirect pathway of hepatic glycogenesis is dependent on the glucose infusion rate, and thus on the prevailing plasma glucose concentration.

the relative contribution to hepatic glycogen repletion via direct and indirect pathways depends on the plasma glucose concentration and that the direct pathway is of minor significance at plasma glucose concentrations that normally prevail after a meal.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the direct pathway of hepatic glycogenesis in vivo and indicates that this pathway plays only a minor role in glycogen repletion in the fed state
the regulation of glycogen synthesis and the relative contribution of two distinct pathways of hepatic glucose storage, i.e. the indirect and direct pathways.
the regulation of hepatic glycogenesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
hepatic glycogen repletion is predominantly mediated by the indirect pathway at physiological plasma glucose concentrations.
the direct and indirect pathway of hepatic glycogenesis are both operative and that the direct pathway becomes increasingly more important as the plasma glucose concentration is elevated.

, at low rates of glucose infusion (0-20 mumol X min X kg-1), the rate of hepato-glycogen synthesis is determined by the rate of appearance of glucose into plasma and that at high rates of glucose infusion, the rate of glycogenesis is determined by the glucose load.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the direct pathway of hepatic glycogenesis is a quantitatively insignificant pathway of glycogen synthesis in vivo and is activated by hyperglycemia, whereas the indirect pathway is activated in the fed state.

the direct pathway of hepatic glycogenesis is activated at high plasma glucose concentrations and that this pathway is quantitatively less important than the indirect pathway of hepatic glucose storage.

the indirect pathway of liver glycogenesis is the major pathway of glycogen synthesis at plasma glucose concentrations below 10-12 mM and the direct pathway becomes increasingly important as plasma glucose concentrations are increased.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the liver is not the only organ that can synthesize glycogen from glucose, and that the liver can synthesize glycogens from glucose in a direct and indirect manner.
hepatic glycogen storage is not dependent on the glucose infusion rate but on the plasma glucose concentration.
hepatic glycogen repletion is primarily achieved via the indirect pathway, even at high glucose concentrations.
